body:
My message must not have shown up right here it is, hopefully it will
work.



This is a reply to the "Unabomber" faq.

While I, and many others sympathetic to FCs cause, appreciate the
effort put forth towards making this document, I find some disturbing
things in it.

In the answer of question number 2 it states:

"It is unknown how many people are members of FC, but some have
   suggested that thousands of people individually share the basic
ideas expressed in the Manifesto and are working towards similar goals. Some
   people have suggested that revolutionaries working toward the same
   goals as FC should consider themselves part of the organization."

I find this rather disturbing.  In the Manifesto it states (94):

"Freedom means being in control (either as an individual or as a
member of a SMALL group)"

Later in that same paragraph:

"One does not have freedom if anyone else (especially a large
organization)"

While the paragraph continues it does not matter in this issue.  My
POINT is this, I consider a small group as no more than a couple
hundred people.  If, and I believe there are, thousands of people
that share the same ideas they should not be considered part of FC.
Instead, let those that believe NOT in the "Unabomber" but in the
MANIFESTO, to create organizations of there own.  This will keep
AUTONOMY while increasing the forces necessary to bring down the
Industrial system.

My next qualm is:

It is stated in the answer to question 3:

"I am an interested ex-scholar who believes in the
   right to free speech, and in exercising my constitutional right"

While I understand there are people with different levels of
commitment to the ideals of the MANIFESTO, I just wish to point out
that the Constitution merely helps the Industrial system.  Refer to
paragraphs 95-98.

I CONGRATULATE the author on question number 4 and how he answered it.

I also congratulate the author on how he answered all questions
regarding POLITICAL affiliation.  Please remember paragraph 94 and
the last sentence.  "It is improtant not to confuse freedom with mere
 permisiveness."  Read the rest of the paragraph to better understand
 what I am talking about.  Also remember which I think the author did
(this is mainly for the readers) that there are different levels of
belief and therefore some people that affiliate with us will belong

to the dictatorial parties.

I congratulate the author on the response to number 8.

On number 10 the author refers to buying the MANIFESTO from Jolly
Roger Press.  While some readers may think that this is against our
ideals, I disagree.  It has made quoting of the manifesto easier and
is easier to carry around.  Their response would be that this is
 another piece of technology that is helping not hurting you.  (One of
 my favorite sections in the manifesto is the one regarding the chess
players.)  While this is true it helping us in our efforts to utilize
the communication system to start the revolution.

I strongly disagree with the choice of including media sites in the
faq.  Throughout the fag the author has been talking harshly of the
media, I share the same views.  While it is important to be educated
(for the revolution), the media is an part of the Industrial system.
 Many readers will be confused and I personally think that it is
outrageous.


I thank the author for writing the faq and hope that he/she will
consider making the necessary changes he/she sees fit.

Jason

"We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system."
